title: One bale’s journey
look: Route map: warm documentary footage full-bleed, a gold route bar along the top fills station by station (5 stations).

beats.vo: This is a bale of paddy straw. A month ago, it was standing in a field in Punjab. Here is where it goes next.
beats.visual: Push-in on a single paddy-straw bale. Hook text: WHERE DOES THIS BALE GO?

beats.vo: After the harvest, a baler presses the loose straw into tight bales, so it can be moved instead of burned.
beats.visual: Baler packing straw in the field. Route bar appears; station 1 BALER lights.

beats.vo: An aggregator collects bales from dozens of farms and stacks them at a depot, dry and covered.
beats.visual: Bales stacked under cover at a depot. Station 2 AGGREGATOR.

beats.vo: From there, a truck takes them to a pellet plant. The straw is shredded, dried, and pressed into small, dense pellets.
beats.visual: Loaded truck on a rural highway, then pellets pouring from the mill. Station 3 PELLET PLANT.

beats.vo: The pellets are tested. Heat value. Moisture. Ash. Then they are loaded for a power plant that must burn biomass along with coal.
beats.visual: Pellets close-up; three spec chips tick in: HEAT VALUE · MOISTURE · ASH. Cut to plant at dusk. Station 4-5.

beats.vo: One bale. Five businesses. Farmer, baler, aggregator, pellet maker, buyer. Every link has to find the next one.
beats.visual: Five role cards (farmer, baler, aggregator, pellet maker, buyer) snap into a chain; links glow one by one.

beats.vo: That is the chain IndiaBiomass is being built to connect.
beats.visual: Chain resolves into the IndiaBiomass mark, end card.

title: Four myths
look: Flip cards: each myth is a card with a red MYTH stamp that flips to a green FACT side; darkened footage behind; counter 1/4 to 4/4.

beats.vo: Four things people get wrong about the biomass business.
beats.visual: Hook text: 4 THINGS PEOPLE GET WRONG ABOUT BIOMASS over quick 3-shot montage.

beats.vo: Myth one. Biomass is just waste. Fact. Once it is collected, dried and processed, it is a fuel, with a spec sheet, a price, and buyers waiting for it.
beats.visual: MYTH 1 card over a residue heap; flips to FACT over bagged fuel, with a mini spec-sheet + price-tag icon.

beats.vo: Myth two. Only big companies can sell to power plants. Fact. Many tenders are open to smaller suppliers, and registered M-S-Es can often skip the deposit.
beats.visual: MYTH 2 card over a small workshop; FACT side shows a tender notice with an M-S-E badge.

beats.vo: Myth three. All straw is the same. Fact. Moisture, ash and heat value decide what your fuel is worth. Buyers test every load.
beats.visual: MYTH 3 over three different residue textures; FACT side: three gauges (moisture, ash, heat) at different levels.

beats.vo: Myth four. The price is whatever the buyer says. Fact. Prices change by region and by season. The real problem is that most sellers cannot see them.
beats.visual: MYTH 4 over a busy market; FACT side: India map with region dots pulsing at different sizes and a season dial (no numbers).

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is building one place to see suppliers, tenders and prices across India.
beats.visual: Cards stack into the IndiaBiomass card; end card.

title: Pellet or briquette?
look: Split screen: the frame is cut vertically, PELLET left and BRIQUETTE right with a VS chip; a scoreboard fills row by row.

beats.vo: Pellet or briquette. Both are pressed biomass, but they are not the same product.
beats.visual: Hook: PELLET or BRIQUETTE? Both halves slide in, VS chip lands.

beats.vo: Pellets are small, about the size of a pencil stub. They flow easily and feed automatically, which is why power plants co-firing biomass mostly ask for pellets.
beats.visual: Left half grows to 70%: pellets pouring; pencil-stub size comparison; row SIZE / FEEDING ticks; power-plant icon.

beats.vo: Briquettes are bigger, like short logs. They are popular with industrial boilers, brick kilns and factories.
beats.visual: Right half grows: briquette logs; icons for boiler, brick kiln, factory.

beats.vo: Pellets need finer, drier raw material and more processing, so a pellet plant costs more to set up. Briquette machines are simpler, which makes them an easier place to start.
beats.visual: Scoreboard rows: RAW MATERIAL (fine & dry vs coarser), PLANT COST (higher vs simpler), with machinery footage in each half.

beats.vo: So which one should you make? It depends on two things. The raw material you have, and who is buying near you.
beats.visual: Question card: WHICH ONE SHOULD YOU MAKE? Two answer chips: YOUR RAW MATERIAL + BUYERS NEAR YOU.

beats.vo: Pellet makers, briquette makers, and the buyers for both. IndiaBiomass is bringing them together.
beats.visual: Both halves merge into the logo; end card.

title: Biomass map of India
look: Map flight: the India map fills the screen; the camera flies to each region, a photo chip pops out of the state with the residue name.

beats.vo: India does not have one kind of biomass. It has a different one in almost every region.
beats.visual: Full India map, all regions glow in different colours. Hook: WHAT DOES YOUR STATE GROW?

beats.vo: In Punjab and Haryana, it is paddy straw, left behind after the rice harvest.
beats.visual: Fly to Punjab & Haryana; chip: PADDY STRAW.

beats.vo: In Rajasthan, mustard husk.
beats.visual: Fly to Rajasthan; chip: MUSTARD HUSK (mustard field footage in chip).

beats.vo: Across Gujarat and Maharashtra, cotton stalks and groundnut shells.
beats.visual: Gujarat & Maharashtra; chips: COTTON STALKS, GROUNDNUT SHELLS.

beats.vo: In Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, bagasse from the sugar mills.
beats.visual: Uttar Pradesh & Maharashtra; chip: BAGASSE (sugarcane footage).

beats.vo: In the South, coconut shells. And rice husk, wherever rice is milled.
beats.visual: South; chips: COCONUT SHELLS, RICE HUSK.

beats.vo: Every one of these is a fuel, if it reaches the right buyer. The problem is distance. The straw is in one state, the factory that needs it is in another, and neither knows the other exists.
beats.visual: Long highway footage; a dashed line stretches between two far-apart pins: SUPPLY ↔ DEMAND.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is mapping who has what, and where, so supply and demand can finally find each other. Which one grows near you?
beats.visual: Pins connect across the map, logo; prompt WHICH ONE GROWS NEAR YOU? (comments).

title: What buyers check
look: Inspection sheet: light paper background with forest-green ink (the only light reel); footage sits in rounded frames; five checkboxes tick down a clipboard.

beats.vo: Before a buyer pays for your biomass, they check five things. Know them before you quote.
beats.visual: Clipboard slides up: 5 CHECKS BEFORE A BUYER PAYS YOU.

beats.vo: One. Moisture. Wet fuel burns poorly, and you end up transporting water. Most buyers set a maximum.
beats.visual: ☐ MOISTURE ticks; frame: water on grain / wet material.

beats.vo: Two. G-C-V. The heat your fuel gives per kilo. Below the minimum, the load can be rejected, or the price cut.
beats.visual: ☐ G-C-V ticks; frame: clean flame; mini gauge with MIN mark.

beats.vo: Three. Ash. More ash means more cleaning, and more wear on the boiler.
beats.visual: ☐ ASH ticks; frame: ash falling.

beats.vo: Four. Size. Pellets and briquettes must match the size the buyer's feeding system takes.
beats.visual: ☐ SIZE ticks; frame: measuring / uniform pellets; caliper icon.

beats.vo: Five. Consistency. One good sample is not enough. Every truck has to match the spec.
beats.visual: ☐ CONSISTENCY ticks; frame: row of identical trucks / conveyor.

beats.vo: Get these five right, and price talks get a lot easier. Screenshot this before your next quote.
beats.visual: Full clipboard, all five ticked; SCREENSHOT THIS stamp.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass. Connecting India's biomass economy.
beats.visual: Logo on paper; end card.

title: The harvest window
look: Two endings: a countdown ring runs the whole reel; the first half is grey and hazy, then the film rewinds and replays in warm gold.

beats.vo: The rice is cut. The clock starts.
beats.visual: Combine harvester cutting paddy; countdown ring starts. Text: THE CLOCK STARTS.

beats.vo: In north India, farmers have only a few weeks between the paddy harvest and sowing wheat. The field has to be cleared. And the straw left behind is bulky, loose, and slow to move.
beats.visual: Ring shows A FEW WEEKS; loose straw over the field; colours drain to grey.

beats.vo: Without a baler, a buyer, or a truck, the fastest option is a matchstick. That is why the smoke comes back every autumn.
beats.visual: Match strike close-up, then haze over farmland at dusk (grey grade).

beats.vo: Now, the same straw, with a plan.
beats.visual: Rewind effect (scan lines run backwards); colour returns gold. Text: WITH A PLAN.

beats.vo: The harvest ends. A baler arrives and packs the straw. Within days, an aggregator picks it up. The field is clear in time for wheat. The straw becomes pellets. The pellets go to a plant that needs them.
beats.visual: Tractor at golden hour, then wheat sown straight into the cleared field. Ring ticks with icons: BALER · AGGREGATOR · CLEAR FIELD.

beats.vo: Same field. Same few weeks. A different ending. What decides it is whether the farmer can find a baler and a buyer in time.
beats.visual: Split: grey ending vs gold ending side by side. Text: SAME FIELD. DIFFERENT ENDING.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is building that connection.
beats.visual: Logo; end card.

title: Guess the biomass
look: Quiz show: a big number, a blurred extreme close-up with a 3-2-1 timer ring, then a pull-back reveal with the name and a score dot.

beats.vo: Four close-ups. Guess what each one is. The answer comes after each.
beats.visual: Hook: GUESS THE BIOMASS · 4 CLOSE-UPS; four blurred tiles.

beats.vo: Number one. Fine, golden and light. It comes off the grain at a rice mill. Rice husk. A common boiler fuel, because it is dry and already collected in one place.
beats.visual: #1 blurred rice husk → reveal RICE HUSK; context shot of a rice mill.

beats.vo: Number two. Pale and fibrous. It is what is left after the juice is pressed out of sugarcane. Bagasse. Many sugar mills burn it to power themselves.
beats.visual: #2 blurred bagasse → reveal BAGASSE; sugarcane crushing context.

beats.vo: Number three. Light, papery pieces, left after threshing a winter oilseed. Mustard husk. Common across Rajasthan.
beats.visual: #3 blurred mustard husk → reveal MUSTARD HUSK.

beats.vo: Number four. Hard, curved and brown. Mostly from the South. Coconut shell. Dense, and also made into charcoal.
beats.visual: #4 blurred coconut shell → reveal COCONUT SHELL.

beats.vo: How many did you get? Tell us in the comments.
beats.visual: Four revealed tiles in a grid; HOW MANY DID YOU GET? comment prompt.

beats.vo: Every one of these has a buyer somewhere. IndiaBiomass is building the way to find them.
beats.visual: Logo; end card.

title: Why we’re building IndiaBiomass
look: Noise to signal: starts loud and cluttered (generic chat bubbles, missed calls, ringing phone), then everything clears into quiet type on forest green and real IndiaBiomass screens.

beats.vo: Ask anyone in the biomass trade how they find a buyer. A phone call. A friend of a friend. A WhatsApp group with a thousand unread messages.
beats.visual: Person on phone; generic chat bubbles and missed-call chips pile up (no WhatsApp branding).

beats.vo: Ask them how they know the right price. Most will tell you they don't. They find out after the deal.
beats.visual: Price tag with a question mark; text: THEY FIND OUT AFTER THE DEAL.

beats.vo: Meanwhile, power plants need fuel every day. Factories are switching their boilers. Farmers have straw with nowhere to go.
beats.visual: Three quick shots: power plant, factory boiler, farmer with straw.

beats.vo: The demand is real. The supply is real. What is missing is the link between them. So we are building it.
beats.visual: Noise clears; two dots (SUPPLY, DEMAND) and a missing link that draws itself. SO WE ARE BUILDING IT.

beats.vo: Verified suppliers and buyers, in one place. Tenders, as they are published. Prices, region by region. Supply and policy updates, tracked for you.
beats.visual: Four feature cards from the real site captures: verified listings, tenders, prices, supply & policy.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass. The information and trust layer for India's biomass industry.
beats.visual: Logo with descriptor; end card.
